Purpose: Fully documented, live-accurate system description for players and GMs
Source of truth: Live throughput wiring and console logic, not legacy JSON
Format: Hybrid mechanic tables + Mal translation + drift flags

📘 1. WHAT A RAID IS

TermCanon DefinitionPlayer-Facing Explanation
RaidA structured, competitive operation between factions or scenarios using OP and Maneuvers“War is not chaos — it’s law with dice rules.”
AssaultDirect attack on enemy hex or position“Kick the door down.”
SiegeEncircle + attrition“Starve the walls, then the spirit.”
InfiltrationStealth (Intrigue) (Intrigue)-based penetration with alarm“Shadows whisper before steel.”
EspionageInformation theft/sabotage“Knowledge is itself a blade.”
CourtlySocial influence battle“Masks, words, and favors win what swords cannot.”
BlockadeEconomic pressure raid“Cut the lifelines.”
PropagandaNarrative / softpower pressure“Belief is a battlefield.”
RitualMetaphysical raid (e.g., Tikkun effects)“Ritual sears reality.”

Drift Flag:
Some old JSON tags (e.g., espionage_legacy) are not present at runtime — only normalized keys are used now.

📈 2. RAID ROUND FLOW (Live Canon)

From engine sequence — confirmed live:

StepWhat HappensMal Translation
1Stage OP“Collect your breathe, summon your resolve.”
2Select Maneuvers“Your gambits line up on the chalkboard.”
3Commit“There is no take-back.”
4Roll + Bonus“Chance tilts the field.”
5Cancel / Reflection Layer“Someone threw sand in the gears.”
6Throughput Preview / Intents“See the dominoes before they fall.”
7resolveRaidRound“World mutates to your action.”
8Post–Round Effects (Morale / Unity / Victory)“The world breathes with your deed.”
9OP Transfers Processed“Energy moves where it must.”
10Round Flags Set“Who has the initiative next?”

Live Canon Rule:

Every 2 staged OP = +1 to your dice, rounding up.

Mal Voice:

“Momentum grows in twos — never alone.”

📍 Outcome Thresholds (Live Canon)

ResultConditionNotes
Failmargin < 0The argument didn’t convince or the blow failed.
Successmargin ≥ 0The push worked.
Great SuccessSpecial tier (from console layer)Not native to raw margin; passed in by console logic.

Important:
The core engine (resolveRaidRound) evaluates success via margin check.
Great Success is a tier state applied earlier in UI logic, not via an engine hard threshold.

Mal Voice:

“Victory has grades, not absolutes.”

🧠 4. CANCEL & REFLECTION LAYER — HOW IT WORKS

Some maneuvers affect others before they land:

reflectEnemyManeuverSends an enemy maneuver backPre-mutation

Order of resolution:

Roll → Throughput intents → Cancel/Reflect adjustments → World Mutation via resolveRaidRound

Mal Translation:

“Before blows land, someone might trip your foot.”

📜 7. ARCHETYPES & SPECIAL SCENARIOS

🔹 Courtly Intrigue

Alternate engine overlay where influence and social pressure replace simple opposed rolls.
This is a layered social combat that uses different scoring and damage logic.

Player Voice:

“In court, words are sharper than blades.”

🔹 Infiltration + Alarm

Not standard roll/opposition.

  • Alarm track increases on failure.

  • Exceeding threshold ends the scenario.

  • Flashback maneuver reduces alarm.

Player Voice:

“The louder you are, the faster guards dance.”

📌 9. RAID SYSTEM — MAL VOICE SUMMARY

“Raid is negotiation by violence — and negotiation by silence.
You bring OP, stage your will, pay the price, roll the die,
and let the world remember who drew first.”

⚔️ RAIDS & STRATEGIC ACTIVITIES

How Factions Force, Shape, and Rewrite the World

The Three Tempos of Power

Bad Eden does not ask whether you have power.
It asks when you are willing to use it — and what kind of future you are buying.

Every meaningful faction action in Bad Eden expresses power at one of three tempos:

TempoSystemWhat You’re Doing
ImmediateRaidsForcing the world to change now
DeferredStrategic Activities (Planner)Making future turns cheaper, safer, and more predictable
Scenario / TranscendentRituals, Courtly Intrigue, InfiltrationNegotiating with systems that do not care about violence

All three:

  • spend OP

  • generate War Logs

  • feed the Turn Engine

  • create consequences

They are not separate subsystems.
They are one engine, played at different speeds.

Planning vs Planner vs Live Raid

Thinking Is Not Commitment

Before we talk about Raids, we need to be precise about three very different modes players interact with:

🔍 Planning Mode (Raid Console)

  • Simulation only

  • No OP spend

  • No War Logs

  • No consequences

Planning Mode exists so you can understand the math before you bleed.

Use it to:

  • test maneuver combinations

  • see projected DCs

  • understand how staging OP affects rolls

📋 Strategic Activities (Planner)

  • Commitment

  • OP is spent when the plan resolves

  • Effects queue to the next Turn

  • Guaranteed outcomes (no dice)

The Planner is not “safe.”
It is quietly dangerous, because it locks your future.

⚔️ Live Raids

  • Immediate OP spend

  • Dice-driven outcomes

  • Morale, Unity, Darkness, and territory change right now

A Live Raid is you telling the world:
“I am willing to pay interest.”

Raids: Forcing the World to Change

A Raid is not an attack roll.
A Raid is two OP engines colliding.

When you declare a Raid, you are committing to:

  • immediate OP expenditure

  • visible escalation

  • outcomes that propagate across multiple systems

How a Raid Resolves (At a Glance)

  1. Declaration

    • Choose Raid Type (Assault, Infiltration, Blockade, Liberation, etc.)

    • Spend 1 OP of the Raid’s primary category to enter the round

  2. Staging

    • Additional OP may be staged

    • Every 2 staged OP = +1 to the roll (rounded up)

  3. Maneuvers

    • Both sides select maneuvers

    • Maneuvers cost OP

    • Maneuvers modify rolls, damage, conditions, or future rounds

  4. Resolution

    • Contested roll (attacker vs defender) or roll vs DC

    • Margin matters:

      • Fail

      • Success

      • Great Success (large margin)

  5. Aftermath

    • Territory changes

    • Morale shifts

    • Unity awarded or lost

    • Effects queued to the next Turn

Player Truth:
Raids are expensive because they solve problems quickly.
They are dangerous because they also create new ones.

Maneuvers: Doctrine, Not Buttons

Maneuvers are not “moves.”
They are doctrines — statements about how your faction fights.

Each maneuver:

  • has a tier (T1–T4)

  • has a rarity

  • has explicit OP costs

  • applies only to certain Raid Types

  • may or may not be available to defenders

What Maneuvers Actually Do

Maneuvers can:

  • reroll dice

  • add or remove tags (Fortified, Alarm, Scandal, etc.)

  • negate damage

  • refund OP

  • rewrite the outcome of a round

  • push Darkness, Unity, or Victory

Higher-tier maneuvers are not “better.”
They are riskier statements about identity.

Using Qliphothic Gambit is not about winning a roll.
It’s about deciding what kind of scars you’re willing to carry.

Strategic Activities: Winning Without Rolling

Strategic Activities are what disciplined factions do instead of panicking.

When you use the Planner, you are:

  • spending OP now

  • queuing effects for the next Turn

  • shaping the map without dice

  • lowering future costs

What Strategic Activities Excel At

Strategic Activities:

  • advance Integration

  • remove negative modifiers

  • add Loyalty, Morale, and Defense

  • build logistics scaffolding

  • stabilize territory

  • create long-term advantages

They do not:

  • flip control instantly

  • end conflicts dramatically

  • satisfy bloodlust

Player Truth:
If Raids win wars, Strategic Activities win empires.

Wilderness Development: From Nothing to Heartland

This is the canonical development loop, and it is almost entirely Planner-driven.

Step 1 — Establish Outpost

  • Claim a wilderness hex

  • Status: Occupied

  • Integration +1

  • Upkeep begins immediately

Step 2 — Develop Outpost (Stability)

  • Remove Hostile / Unrest

  • Add Patrols / Infrastructure

  • Loyalty & Morale increase

  • Integration +1

Step 3 — Upgrade to Settlement

  • Size increases

  • Status becomes Claimed

  • Resources begin to matter

  • Integration +1

Step 4 — Found Sites

  • Farm, Mine, Port, Temple, Research, Fortress

  • Hex identity becomes concrete

  • Integration +1 per development

Step 5 — Integrated Heartland

  • Upkeep drops

  • Bonuses activate

  • Unity becomes possible

Critical Insight (Soul) (Soul):
Raids open territory.
Planning is how you keep it.

Soft Power vs Hard Power

The Math Behind the Myth

Hard power:

  • changes ownership

  • increases visibility

  • raises upkeep

  • attracts retaliation

Soft power:

  • reduces costs

  • stabilizes populations

  • increases net OP

  • prevents future raids

Strategic Activities like:

  • Loyalty Programs

  • Diplomatic Missions

  • Cultural Festivals

  • Policy Reforms

…often cost less OP than the penalties they prevent.

Player Truth:
Violence is loud.
Soft power is compound interest.

Scenarios as Power

When Violence Is the Wrong Language

Some conflicts are not about territory.

Courtly Intrigue (Social Combat)

  • Influence Integrity replaces Structure

  • Diplomacy, Soft Power, Intrigue, and Violence all matter

  • OP spent becomes arguments

  • Scandal, Backlash, and Reputation replace casualties

Victory here:

  • grants Unity

  • shifts faction trajectories

  • changes who the world listens to

Infiltration (Alarm-Based)

  • No “win roll”

  • Alarm escalates through bands

  • Failure creates future danger

  • Flashbacks allow OP to rewrite mistakes

Player Truth:
These scenarios punish brute force.
They reward restraint and timing.

Transference Across All Three Systems

OP does not only come from territory.

It can be forced into existence by sacrifice.

Valid fuels include:

  • Integrity

  • Clarity points

  • Stress

  • Pool Dice

This is not free power.
It is burning future potential to act now.

Metaphysical Truth:
OP is not generated.
It is redirected from what could have been.

When the World Pushes Back

Every aggressive action increases:

  • Visibility

  • Pressure

  • Darkness

  • Expectations

Raids:

  • affect Morale immediately

  • affect Unity by outcome

  • shape Victory trajectories

Strategic Actions:

  • quietly raise or lower the ceiling

  • determine whether the world trusts your faction

Bad Eden does not punish you for acting.
It punishes you for acting without a plan.

Story Pair: Two Factions, One Choice

🟢 The Patient Architect

  • Uses Planner early

  • Raids sparingly

  • Integrates before expanding

  • Wins fewer battles

  • Never collapses

🔴 The Reckless Hammer

  • Raids constantly

  • Ignores upkeep

  • Solves every problem with force

  • Wins spectacularly

  • Falls apart quietly

The difference was never luck.
It was tempo.

Final Truth

Raids decide what happens.
Strategic Activities decide how much it costs.
Rituals decide what the world believes is possible.

Master Bad Eden by learning when to use each —
and you will never feel like the game is unfair.

🎭 COURTLY INTRIGUE — SOCIAL COMBAT ENGINE

“In court, steel is vulgar. Influence bleeds quieter.”

Courtly is not a margin ≥ 0 opposed roll.

It is an Influence Integrity duel.
